newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea prices steady on brisk buying.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea prices steady on brisk buying.

text.p: Keen buying ahead of the upcoming quality season -- when demand for Ceylon tea soars -- kept prices buoyant at Wednesday's Colombo auction, brokers said.
"The quality season will be upon us by the middle of next month, when quantity comes down and prices soar. A lot of people were buying up before then," said a broker for Eastern Brokers.
Much of the demand for the high quantity of 5.9 million kg on offer came from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), which was purchasing for winter, brokers said.
The island's distinct low growns saw widespread demand at lower levels. High growns were all dearer, brokers Forbes and Walker said.
The anticipated average auction price was 120 rupees per kg, compared with 120.3 rupees last week, Forbes said.
The weekly sale average last went over 120 rupees on October 23, 1996 on strong winter demand from the CIS, the biggest buyer of Ceylon tea.
Sri Lankan tea prices peaked at the October 16, 1996 auction when the weekly average price hit an all-time high of 124.08 rupees.
The next auction is on July 1-2 where six million kg will be on offer.
